choices.scope: EIA's Data Center Servers service (80 TWh in 2023) is narrower than LBNL's whole-facility count (176 TWh). EIA's service is scaled by that 2023 ratio to compare like with like. Check: scaled EIA in 2028 is 323 TWh, against LBNL's low end of 325.
choices.gw_to_twh: GW times 8.76 times the 82% load factor, for every forecast given in GW. Forecasts that are capacity or peak are treated alike.
choices.added: Only the part above EIA's own scaled path is added, to commercial electricity. It runs flat across the hours of the year.
choices.between_anchors: Straight lines between anchors, starting from EIA's scaled 2025 level.
choices.after_last_anchor: No source goes further, so the amount added is held at its last anchor year's level; the total keeps growing only with EIA's own path.
choices.non_ai_load: The 50 GW is AI only. Everything else is held at the 2025 level through 2028.
choices.flexibility: Duke's 0.5% is applied as a budget on the added load's energy in each region; the dispatch LP spends it where power is scarcest or dearest. 3-hour blocks, so the short curtailments Duke describes are coarser here.
choices.fleet: The LP runs EIA's reference plant fleet and builds nothing, so load the fleet cannot meet is reported as unserved. That number says how much would have to be built, not that the lights go out. Unserved load burns no fuel, so CO2 in these cases is a floor.
